findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: static_map, map_setup · Private data: static_map, privacy_area_map · Public sink: district_lookup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: static_map, map_setup · Private data: static_map, privacy_area_map · Public sink: district_lookup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "district_lookup" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "List the Texas special taxing districts that contain a latitude/longitude: municipal utility districts (MUD), water control and improvement districts (WCID), fresh water supply, levee and management districts statewide (TCEQ), and public improvement districts (PID) where cities publish them (coverag" → after: "List the Texas special taxing districts that contain a latitude/longitude: municipal utility districts (MUD), water control and improvement districts (WCID), fresh water supply, levee and management districts statewide (TCEQ), and public improvement districts (PID) where cities publish them (coverag"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
